title: getCounterAttackChance sums tiered adds, making every predator counter-attack a guaranteed kill (1.0 chance)
impact: Whenever Iron Spears has been forged (or Iron Swords researched), both nodes are researched, so researchedEffect(...,'add') returns 0.45 + 0.55 = 1.0 and this function returns 1.0. rollCounterAttack (combat.ts:157-159) computes roll = (hash % 1000)/1000 in [0, 0.999] and returns roll < chance, so it is always true: in tickLayerSystems.ts:394-403 every predator contact (Wolf, Fox, and the cursed Moon Howler) kills the predator instead of the settler, making predator deaths of settlers impossible late game. The explicit 0.55 / 0.45 fallback on line 133 is unreachable. getPredatorBlockChance (117-122) accumulates the same way (0.35 + 0.6 + 0.72 = 1.67); its Math.min(0.85, chance) cap masks the sum and makes the tier Math.max chance,0.72/0.6/0.35 branches dead, so the applied block rate is the cap rather than the researched tier.
fix: Treat these as tier effects, not additive stacks: resolve the highest researched tier (e.g. if (hasIronSwords(state)) return 0.55; if (hasIronSpears(state)) return 0.45;) and keep any researched-effect override capped, e.g. return Math.min(0.85, add). Re-check getPredatorBlockChance after the same change.

Fix: `if (add !== undefined) return Math.min(hasIronSwords(state) ? 0.55 : 0.45, add);`. High: guaranteed predator kills are a clearly wrong, player-visible combat outcome, but no state corruption.

title: tryGraduateHumanChild is unreachable: the daily age sync clears isJuvenile before the graduation check, so no child ever graduates
evidence: dayCycle.ts:135 `if (!entity.isJuvenile || entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS) return false;` — but dayCycle.ts:246 in the sync that runs first sets `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS;`, and humanTick.ts runs the sync at line 300 (`syncHumanAgeFromCalendar(entity, state, {...})`) before the check at line 360 (`tryGraduateHumanChild(entity, config.size, config.speed, (e) => { if (isPlayerHuman(e)) applyEducationGraduation(state, e); });`).
impact: `computeHumanAgeYears` returns 12 exactly when daysLived reaches juvenileSpan, and line 246 immediately sets isJuvenile=false, so on the only tick where age>=HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS the guard's `!entity.isJuvenile` clause is already true and the body never runs. No human is ever incremented out of juvenile by this function (only setHumanBirthFromAge/syncHumanAgeFromCalendar ever write isJuvenile — verified by grep; tickLayerSystems.ts:227 only handles WILDLIFE_TICK_TYPES, which excludes Human). Consequence: `applyEducationGraduation` (only other reference is its definition, education.ts:125) is never called, so `entity.educated` is never set — schoolDays accumulated as a juvenile never convert to skill/energy bonuses, no 'Graduation' notification/event ever fires, and `getEducationResearchMultiplier` (education.ts:155) can never count an educated settler. `entity.size` also stays at the juvenile 0.5x value set in entityFactory.ts:110 (today the renderer derives human scale from isJuvenile, so this is latent rather than visible).
fix: Let the graduation transition own the flag: in `syncHumanAgeFromCalendar` (dayCycle.ts:246) stop clearing `isJuvenile` and instead pass the new age to the promotion owner — e.g. make the sync return `wasJuvenile && !isNowJuvenile`, or delete line 246 and have `tryGraduateHumanChild` (called every tick from humanTick.ts:360) clear `isJuvenile` together with size/speed and the `onGraduate` callback. Do not simply drop the `!entity.isJuvenile` clause, or every adult would re-run the callback each tick.
verification: Verified by running gameTick on a settler born 359.7 days earlier with schoolDays=20: at the day boundary age became 12 and isJuvenile false (syncHumanAgeFromCalendar via humanTick.ts:300 → dayCycle.ts:245-246) while `educated` stayed undefined, and a later direct tryGraduateHumanChild call returned false. The two guard clauses are mutually exclusive because entity.age only reaches HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS through that same sync (grep: isJuvenile is written only by setHumanBirthFromAge, syncHumanAgeFromCalendar, tryGraduate, finalizeSettlerAge and migrateHumanAges), so applyEducationGraduation (education.ts:125) is dead and `educated` is never set. Minimal fix: let the graduation transition own the flag — remove the isJuvenile write at dayCycle.ts:246 (have the sync report the transition) and let tryGraduateHumanChild, called every tick from humanTick.ts:360, clear isJuvenile/size/speed with the callback exactly once.

title: Event-log id allocator is per-realm and is never re-synced when a world is handed to the worker, so worker chronicle entries are dropped by the delta dedupe
evidence: L4: `let nextEventLogId = 1;`  L12: `nextEventLogId = Math.max(...state.eventLog.map((e) => e.id)) + 1;`  L24: `id: nextEventLogId++,` — the only callers of `syncEventLogIdFromState` are `saveLoad.ts:445` and `worldGen.ts:683` (both main thread). The worker entry points `simPrep.ts:245 world.eventLog = prep.eventLog;` and `gameWorker.ts:118-124 resetWorkerSession` never call it, and `SimPrepPayload` carries `eventLog` (simPrep.ts:67,161) but no id counter.
impact: Any freshly created (or recovered) worker starts allocating ids from 1 while the imported log already holds ids 1..N (N = entries in the save, up to the 2000 cap). `applySimTickDelta` skips tail entries whose id already exists (`simDelta.ts:513 if (!existingIds.has(entry.id))`), so the first N events the worker logs never reach the display copy: after loading a mid/late game the in-game Chronicle silently freezes for hundreds-to-thousands of events even though the simulation keeps logging. The same untracked counter is used by the optimistic display path (`gameLoop.ts:540-542 applyWorkerCommand` on a clone of the worker's shadow world), which can allocate an id that the worker has already used, producing duplicate ids in one log (duplicate React `key={evt.id}` in EventLogPanel.tsx:197).
fix: Make the allocator travel with the log: add `import { syncEventLogIdFromState } from '../eventLog';` to `simPrep.ts` and call `syncEventLogIdFromState(world)` immediately after `world.eventLog = prep.eventLog;` (L245) — alternatively call it in `gameWorker.ts resetWorkerSession` (L118-124) so the worker's ids continue above the restored log.
verification: `nextEventLogId` is module-scoped (4) and `syncEventLogIdFromState` has only the two main-thread callers saveLoad.ts:445 and worldGen.ts:683, while `resetWorkerSession` (gameWorker.ts:118-124) installs the imported world — whose `eventLog` carries ids 1..N from the save — without resyncing, so a fresh worker allocates ids from 1 again (24). `applySimTickDelta` skips incoming tail entries whose id already exists in the display log (simDelta.ts:504-517), so after loading a save in worker mode the main-thread Chronicle silently ignores the worker's new entries until its counter passes the saved maximum (up to the 2000-entry cap), while the worker's own log holds duplicate ids; tests/simDelta.eventLog.test.ts only uses non-colliding ids and does not lock the allocator. Fix: import and call `syncEventLogIdFromState(world)` in the worker right after the world is installed (`simPrep.ts:245` or preferably `gameWorker.resetWorkerSession`), or compute the next id from `state.eventLog` inside `logEvent`.

title: buildHousingUnits merges adult children into the parents' housing unit, so the adult-child move-out is undone inside the same assignMissingResidences call
evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.
fix: Add the missing guard at the top of the bucket loop: `if (visited.has(custodianId)) continue;` (and attach that bucket's children to the custodian's existing unit, or rebuild the children buckets from the emitted units) so each settler belongs to exactly one housing unit; the child whose custodian is already in a unit must join that unit rather than fall through to the single-entity fallback at line 283.
verification: The mechanism is real: buildHousingUnits' second loop (residencySelection.ts:283-288) calls collectOwnHousehold, which appends every alive childrenIds entry with no age filter (householdComposition.ts:19), and rebuildChildrenIds (residencyReconciliation.ts:48-54) rebuilds those links for adults too. For a parent with no minor children the unit spans both houses, isFamilyHousingValid fails, and the convergence loop (residencyReconciliation.ts:220-247) unassigns and re-homes the whole unit together, so a lone adult child's move-out never persists; I traced that an adult child who heads their own unit (partner/minor children) does end up split, but only after every call runs all 24 passes. This is exactly the root cause left unresolved in BUG_REPORTS/2026-09-13-move-out-reverted-by-residency-reconciliation.md. Minimal fix: build the second-loop unit as seed + living partner + isMinorChild members only.

title: Legacy Church migration runs on every load and strips the player's assigned priest

title: Affair exposure reason ignores its inputs and always rolls a flat 22% 'caught', which jails and always divorces
evidence: lines 789-799: the affair branch gates only on `hasAffairPartner(entity, ctx.entityById) && entity.energy > ... && !isSpouseNearby(...)` and then rolls `if (Math.random() < HUMAN_DAILY_AFFAIR_PREGNANCY_CHANCE * fertility) {` (line 799). The youth branch directly above instead requires `entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END` (lines 754-755).
impact: isValidAffairTarget (line 622) admits targets from HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16, so a 16-17-year-old single settler can become an established affair partner through the daily owner. tryDailyConception is called for every non-prisoner player human (humanTick.ts:330), so that settler then rolls the full adult affair rate 0.14 x fertility (fertility = 1 up to age 35) - roughly 45x (age 17) to 60x (age 16) the youth-gate chance (0.0045 x 0.50 at 16) - with no mutual youth-love link and no age check, contradicting SIMULATION_AUTHORITY.md section 5: "At ages 14-17 it requires the documented mutual youth-love, nearby, energy, and reduced-probability gate".
fix: Restrict the affair branch to adults, e.g. add `&& !(entity.age >= HUMAN_FERTILITY_START && entity.age < HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END)` to the condition at line 789 (or require `entity.age >= HUMAN_YOUTH_FERTILITY_END`), so ages 14-17 can only conceive through the youth branch.
verification: pickAffairExposureReason (1043-1053) discards `_cheater/_lover/_humans` and returns 'caught' on a flat 22% roll gated only by hasStaffedPrison (1036-1041, any completed prison with a guard anywhere), and both daily-gossip call sites (326, 342) feed that verdict to exposeAffair, where 'caught' arrests both partners (1149-1152) and calls tryDivorceOnCaughtCheater(..., true), whose caughtInAct=true skips the isSpouseNearby gate (982) and forces divorceChance = 1 (986). Because the gossip gate only needs affairProgress ≥ 45/85 and no witness check at all, a pair that is merely gossiped about can be jailed and forcibly divorced with no spouse or guard present while the log asserts they 'were caught'. Fix: make the reason evidence-based inside the helper (spouse/guard proximity from the arguments it already receives) or have the daily gossip path pass 'rumor'.

title: YearlyStats.deaths subtracts a per-year count from a cumulative dead-entity count
evidence:
stats.ts:104 `humans: entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive && e.age > 0).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.humans || 0),`
stats.ts:107 `).length - (prevYearStats?.deaths.animals || 0),`
stats.ts:132 `s.totalHumansDied = state.entities.filter(e => e.type === ET.Human && !e.alive).length;`
gameTick.ts:206-208 `const allAlive: Entity[] = [];` / `for (const e of aliveEntities) {` / `if (e.alive) allAlive.push(e);` then gameTick.ts:234 `state.entities = allAlive;`
impact: gameTick rebuilds `state.entities` from alive entities only, so by the time `recordYearlyStats` runs at the year-rollover tick (gameTick.ts:83) the world array contains no `!alive` entity. `YearlyStats.deaths.humans`/`deaths.animals` are therefore always 0 and `lifetimeStats.totalHumansDied` is always 0, which is what StatisticsPanel.tsx:43 renders as "Humans Died" — the lifetime records panel reports 0 deaths forever. title: pathCache stores origin-dependent waypoint lists under origin-independent keys, so a settler can be steered back to a stale path origin
evidence: 269: `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(128, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));` (comment 268: "Sub-tile sampling steps prevent tunneling through 1-tile diagonal obstacles")
impact: `TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE` is 10 (gameTypes.ts:992) and the intended step is 5px, but the 128 cap makes the real spacing span/128: 11.7px for a full medium-map line (1200x900 -> span ~1500px) and ~25px on a huge map (2560x1920 -> span ~3200px), i.e. larger than the tile itself. A 1-tile river or mountain strip can fall between two samples, so `lineCrossesBlocked` returns false, `steerWithPath` returns 'direct' (316/349) and the human walks straight through water/mountain — the exact failure the module was written to prevent. Humans have no terrain collision (only wildlife has the deep-water guard, tickLayerSystems.ts:609-628), so nothing downstream corrects it.

title: Housing pickers accept rival-camp houses; two callers pass buildings.filter(isResidenceBuilding), which keeps faction 'rival' residences
evidence: residencySelection.ts:267-268 `const unit: Entity[] = [custodian]; visited.add(custodian.id);` — the bucket loop never checks `visited.has(custodianId)` before building the unit (contrast the fallback loop at line 284: `if (visited.has(human.id)) continue;` and the partner guard at line 270 `if (partner && !visited.has(partner.id))`).
impact: Concrete failure: mother M has minor child A (custodian M), father F has minor child B (custodian F, B's mother dead), and M and F are partners (a blended family created by remarriage — reachable through humanTick.ts:910/tryCompleteCourtshipMarriage). Bucket[M]=[A] builds unit [M,F,A] and marks F visited, but bucket[F]=[B] still builds unit [F,B] containing F again. In assignMissingResidences (residencyReconciliation.ts:230-239) every unit that needs reassignment clears and re-places ALL of its members, so F is moved twice per pass and the two units keep stealing him: [F,B] is placed in an empty house, then [M,F,A] (now invalid) is cleared and placed in another empty house, and the 24-pass loop never records `reassigned === 0`, so it runs all 24 passes on every assign pulse (4x/day). The stable end state leaves the minor child B alone in one house while F, M and A occupy another — the exact opposite of assignFamilyToResidence's contract ('keeps children with custodian'); ensureOrphanAdoption cannot repair it because B still has a living natural custodian, so the split persists across pulses.

Fix: add `if (residence.faction === 'rival') continue;` beside the leader-house skip in the three pickers, or pass `listPlayerResidences(buildings)` at both call sites.

title: migrateTickTimeline scales some absolute-tick fields but not pregnancyDueProgress or pendingStoryEvents deadlines

title: Big News ids are re-minted from 1 after a save load while persisted dismissal ids keep the old bn_N — every new card is silently hidden
evidence: simEffects.ts:93 `nextBigNewsId = maxSeq + 1;` driven only by simEffects.ts:86-87 `for (const item of state.bigNews) { const match = /^bn_(\d+)$/.exec(item.id) ...`; simEffects.ts:102-104 `const seq = nextBigNewsId++; state.bigNews.push({ id: \`bn_${seq}\`, ...`. The load path empties that array first: saveLoad.ts:367 `bigNews: [],` then saveLoad.ts:446 `syncBigNewsIdFromState(world);` — while the dismissal ids ARE persisted (saveSchema.ts:22 `'villageForge', 'tutorialSeen', 'dismissedBigNewsIds', ...`) and re-applied as a display filter (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:304-311 `const dismissedIds = new Set(loadedWorld.dismissedBigNewsIds ?? []); ... setHiddenBigNewsIds(dismissedIds);` and :319-321 `.filter((news) => !news.dismissed && !hiddenBigNewsIds.has(news.id))`).
impact: Every big-news card a player dismisses (manually or by the 8s auto-dismiss timer, useTransientGameFeedback.ts:241-244 -> dismissBigNewsItem -> dismissedBigNewsIds) leaves a `bn_N` id in the save. verification: syncBigNewsIdFromState (simEffects.ts:84-94) derives maxSeq only from state.bigNews, and the load path empties that array (saveLoad.ts:367 `bigNews: []`) before calling it at :446, so the module counter restarts at 1 — in the worker too, since gameWorker.ts never calls it (grep finds it only in saveLoad/gameEngine) — while dismissedBigNewsIds is a persisted allow-listed field (saveSchema.ts:22) reused both as a display filter (useTransientGameFeedback.ts:304-311, 319-321) and as a delta filter (simDelta.ts:20-25). title: Off-screen wildlife throttle counts ticks, not wildlife-layer calls, so it was never rescaled for the 72-tick day / 4-tick layer
evidence:
src/game/tickLayerSystems.ts:253-254: `const wildlifeActive = wildlifeInFocus || (state.tick + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0;`
src/game/simFocus.ts:25-26: `/** How often off-screen wildlife runs full AI (every N wildlife-layer calls). */ export const OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE = 8;`
impact: tickWildlife runs only when `state.tick % WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL === 0` (LAYER_SYSTEMS_INTERVAL = 4, gameTick.ts:198), but the throttle is tested against the raw tick, so off-screen fauna get full AI on every second layer pulse (every 8 ticks), not one in eight pulses as the constant's declared unit states. The sibling OFFSCREEN_HUMAN_THROTTLE was explicitly rescaled for TICKS_PER_DAY=72 (8 -> 24, locked by tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts:95-99) but this one was left at 8, so off-screen wildlife decisions per in-game day are 3x the legacy rate (9/day vs 3/day) and the off-screen AI budget is 4x the declared one.
fix: Either count layer pulses (`(Math.floor(state.tick / WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL) + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0`) or keep tick units and set the constant to `8 * TICKS_PER_HOUR`; update the docstring and extend tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts with the wildlife throttle assertion.
verification: gameTick.ts:198 runs tickLayerSystems only when state.tick % 4 === 0, while tickLayerSystems.ts:253-254 tests (state.tick + entity.id) % 8 on the raw tick, and simFocus.ts:25 states the unit as 'every N wildlife-layer calls'; the human sibling was rescaled to 24 and is locked by tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts:95-99. The consequence is worse than the claimed 3x rate: since the layer tick is always a multiple of 4, (tick+id) % 8 === 0 has no solution for ids ≡ 1, 2 or 3 (mod 4), so ~75% of out-of-focus fauna never pass the throttle gate (the `continue` at 255-259 skips movement, hunting, grazing at 526-571 and reproduction at 681-736) while the unconditional metabolic drain at line 242 still runs every pulse — they starve off-camera; the ids that do pass (≡ 0 mod 4) run AI every second pulse, not one in eight. Minimal fix: gate on the layer-pulse index, e.g. (Math.floor(state.tick / WILDLIFE_LAYER_INTERVAL) + entity.id) % OFFSCREEN_WILDLIFE_THROTTLE === 0, or keep tick units and set the constant to 8 * TICKS_PER_HOUR with the docstring corrected, and add the assertion to tests/dayCycle.cadence.test.ts.

title: availableScripts uses eventLog.slice(-40), which is the oldest 40 entries of a newest-first log, not the recent history the comment claims
evidence: 62: `const recent = state.eventLog.slice(-40);` with the local named `recent` and the module comment promising 'script selection from real history' (line 4). eventLog is newest-first: eventLog.ts:23 `state.eventLog.unshift({...})`, and simDelta.ts:236 takes `world.eventLog.slice(0, EVENT_LOG_DELTA_TAIL_MAX)` as the recent tail. `slice(-40)` therefore returns the last 40 entries of the array, i.e. the colony's oldest recorded events.

title: Seasonal festival is cancelled for the whole season when a random festival is still active on its single check day
impact: The comment at lines 46-48 promises '5 days at the start of each season: 20 guaranteed festival days per year', but the seasonal festival has exactly one eligible tick per season and the `!state.festival` condition blocks it whenever a random festival is active. Random festivals last 20-39 days (line 75) and can be running on days 3 (a day-350 start carrying over), 183 (a day-150 start) and 273 (a day-250 start), and there is no retry, so that season's seasonal festival is silently lost - the 'guaranteed' 20 days can be 0, 5 or 10.

Random festivals are rolled every FESTIVAL_CHECK_TICKS = 50 days (69-71; dayCycle.ts:308) and last 20-39 days (line 75), so a festival started on day 150 with ≥33 days left covers day 183 and one started on day 250 with ≥23 days covers day 273 — plausible, not certain, hence low. title: `avoidTreeId` retry loop can never run (no caller supplies it) and, if wired, its stride can be a no-op
evidence: L288-293: `if (avoidTreeId && usePool.length > 1) { for (let attempt = 0; attempt < usePool.length && tree.id === avoidTreeId; attempt++) { index = (index + 5 + entityId) % usePool.length; tree = usePool[index]!; } }` — the only producer of `ChatPickOptions` is `chatHintsFromWorld` (humanChat.ts:94-101), which returns only `{ season, weather, festivalActive, foodLow }`, so `options.avoidTreeId` is always `undefined` at both pass-through sites (humanChat.ts:354, 391).

Separately, if the field were ever populated, the stride `5 + entityId` is `0 mod usePool.length` whenever `pool.length` divides `5 + entityId`, so all `usePool.length` attempts land on the avoided tree and the loop returns it anyway (bounded, but a silent no-op).

verification: Verified: the avoidTreeId parameter (263) and retry block (288-293) are inert because the only producer of ChatPickOptions, chatHintsFromWorld (humanChat.ts:94-101), returns just season/weather/festivalActive/foodLow, and the two pass-through call sites (humanChat.ts:354, 391) forward an always-undefined field; grep finds no other assignment. title: NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS guard can never fire, so valley stage changes are never rate-limited
evidence: ecologyStage.ts:365-368 `const cooldownOk = day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) >= NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS || rising || valleyStageIndex(next) <= valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1;` and line 370 `if (!cooldownOk && !rising) return;`
impact: `announceStage` is only reached when `next !== current` (line 453), and every transition it can produce is exactly one step (line 445 `STAGE_ORDER[Math.min(newIdx, 3)]` with newIdx = currentIdx+1 capped at 2, line 450 `currentIdx - 1`). Therefore `!rising` implies `valleyStageIndex(next) === valleyStageIndex(prev) - 1`, the third disjunct is always true, `cooldownOk` is always true, and the early return at line 370 is unreachable: the 3-day re-notify cooldown and the `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` field it depends on can never suppress a message.
fix: Either drop the third disjunct and gate on the cooldown alone (`if (day - (state.valleyLastStageNotifyDay ?? -999) < NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS) return;`), or delete NOTIFY_COOLDOWN_DAYS, `valleyLastStageNotifyDay` and the guard if one notification per transition is the intent.
verification: announceStage is called only when next !== current (ecologyStage.ts:453), and the only writers of `next` produce exactly one-level moves — up at line 431 (currentIdx + 1, possibly capped down to equal current, in which case announceStage is never called) and down at line 450 (STAGE_ORDER[max(0, currentIdx - 1)]) — so the third disjunct at line 368 is true for every recovery and `rising` for every escalation, making cooldownOk always true. Minimal fix: drop the always-true third disjunct so the cooldown throttles recovery notices, or delete the guard plus the unused constant/field.

title: Juvenile size uses HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE (16) while isJuvenile is later overwritten from HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS (12), producing half-size adults
evidence: entityFactory.ts:66 `isJuvenile ?? (isHuman && opts?.ageYears !== undefined ? opts.ageYears < HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE : false);` with `HUMAN_ADULT_MIN_AGE = 16` (dayCycleConstants.ts:12), used at entityFactory.ts:110 `size: effectiveJuvenile ? config.size * 0.5 : config.size,`; but the same function then calls entityFactory.ts:159 `setHumanBirthFromAge(entity, opts.ageYears, opts.colonyDay ?? 0);`, which recomputes the flag with a different threshold — dayCycle.ts:212 `entity.isJuvenile = entity.age < HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS;` (HUMAN_CHILDHOOD_DAYS = 12, dayCycle.ts:126), and `syncHumanAgeFromCalendar` (dayCycle.ts:246) uses 12 as well.

title: Legacy combat-kind fallback is applied to every chronicle line and classifies any message containing "raid" as a combat event

title: grantRaidSpoils subtracts resources instead of capping when stores are above their storage cap
impact: room is not floored at 0, so when a resource already exceeds its cap a successful outgoing raid or accepted tribute removes that resource. Example: food 1000 with a cap that has dropped to 800 (demolishing a Barn or Silo recomputes caps in economy.ts:8-21 while stores stay put; demolition refunds add resources uncapped in buildingPlacementActions.ts:180-182) - winning a raid with 40 food spoils evaluates Math.min(800-1000, 40) = -200 and drops food to 800. The rest of the codebase floors headroom (resourceUtils.ts:43, VisitorCampPanel.tsx:30) and clampRaidGoldGain already floors gold, so this is an omission, not the established convention.

verification: Lines 682/687/692 compute `room = state.storageMax.X - state.resources.X` with no floor, so when a resource exceeds its cap `gained.X` becomes negative and `state.resources.X += gained.X` silently destroys the overflow and reports a negative loot figure — while resourceUtils.ts:43 and clampRaidGoldGain (line 672) both floor their headroom. Minimal fix: wrap each room term in Math.max(0, ...).

title: Hunting-Spot output reads the research key `hunt_yield`, which no research node defines, so hunt research can never boost it

title: tryFirstWeekVisitor doc comment contradicts its own guard (day 4-7 versus tick window for days 7-13)
evidence: line 1853 `/** Once per game: friendly visitors on day 4–7 if the player has shelter and no camp yet. */` versus line 1861 `if (state.tick < 7 * TICKS_PER_DAY || state.tick >= 14 * TICKS_PER_DAY) return null;`
impact: The comment is the only specification for this once-per-game beat and it is wrong twice: the window is days 7-13, and the 'no camp yet' clause is never tested (the function relies on state.firstWeekVisitorSpawned, line 1859, plus the fact that nothing else can spawn a camp that early). Fix (documentation only): rewrite the comment to state days 7-13, the House/Mansion requirement, and the one-shot flag, and drop the untested "no camp yet" clause.

title: Medicine food cost bypasses the economy ledger
evidence: 156: `if (personDayRoll(doctor.id, state.tick, 901 + best.id) > 0.35) return false;` then 92-95 `const heal = Math.min(..., (8 + strength * 14) * ...)`; 99 `if (state.resources.food >= 1 && Math.random() < 0.25) {`; 107 `gainSkill(state, id, JobType.Doctor, 0.08);`

title: clearEntityChat leaves chatDialogueSessionKey set, so a vanished session leaves the settler flagged dialogue-busy
impact: Callers force phrases without checking isDialogueBusy/chatTicks — e.g. humanLeisureBehavior.ts:100 (`sayHumanChatPhrase(entity, impulse.bubble, 55)`), humanRelationships.ts:1494-1495, townHall.ts:237+, villageLeadership.ts:621. The survivor keeps chatDialogueSessionKey, so isDialogueBusy (60-62) stays true and excludes them from ambient targeting, banter and greetings (humanSocial.ts:61/84, socialLife.ts:349/355/386) until a later chat start overwrites the key; unlike clearDialogueSession (172-189) and cleanupEntityDialogueState (595-596), this path never clears it. title: Prisoner early-exit skips shared per-tick upkeep: chat/dialogue timers freeze and pregnancy progress stops
evidence: humanTick.ts:388-403 `if (isPrisoner) { ... syncEntityGrids(ctx, entity); continue; }` exits the iteration before humanTick.ts:794-801 `if (isPlayerHuman(entity) && entity.gender === 'female' && entity.pregnant && !conceivedToday && entity.pregnancyProgress !== undefined) { tickPregnancyAndBirth(state, ctx, entity, { livingHumanAt }); }`. Pregnancy can coexist with imprisonment: arrest happens in exposeAffair -> arrestForScandal (humanRelationships.ts:1149-1152, 1203) and the daily gossip path only excludes a pregnancy fathered by the lover (humanRelationships.ts:313-318 `if ((entity.pregnant && entity.pregnantById === lover.id) || ...) return;`), so a married woman pregnant by her husband can be arrested as 'caught'.
impact: While imprisoned, `pregnancyProgress` never advances (and the mother also takes no energy loss and no meal), so the term silently stretches by the 2.5-6 day sentence; if a save is taken during that window the progress field and the birth date the player sees diverge from the declared 24-day pregnancy. Any invariant/test that expects a pregnancy to advance every tick while `entity.pregnant` holds is violated for this edge case.
fix: Move the pregnancy gate above the prisoner branch (or run it for prisoners before `continue`), i.e. advance existing pregnancy for imprisoned pregnant settlers while still skipping movement/needs.
verification: The prisoner branch sets velocity, walks to the prison and `continue`s at 402, before `tickHumanChat` (405) and before the pregnancy gate at 794-802; `chatTicks` is decremented only in humanChat.ts:364 and `tickPregnancyAndBirth` has exactly one caller, humanTick.ts:801 (humanLifecycle.ts:63 is the only progress increment), so both really do freeze for the whole sentence. This is reachable in normal play because `exposeAffair` -> `arrestForScandal` (humanRelationships.ts:1149-1152, 1164-1217) can jail a married pregnant settler for `ticksForDays(2.5 + random*3.5)`, delaying the birth past its due progress and leaving a dialogue bubble frozen; no invariant breaks and no test covers prisoners. Fix: hoist `tickHumanChat(entity, resolveChatPartner)` and the pregnancy block above the `if (isPrisoner)` early exit (or call both before the `continue`).
alsoReportedAs: A pregnant prisoner's pregnancy is frozen: the prisoner branch `continue`s before the pregnancy-progress gate, so the term is extended by the whole sentence (A8-humanTick)

title: `canPursueSecretAffair` is called without the colony work schedule, so the realtime affair gate uses the legacy 07:00-16:00 window
evidence: humanTick.ts:220-222 `const nurturingSettlerCount = allHumans.filter((h) => h.alive && !h.isJuvenile && h.traits?.includes('nurturing')).length;` — `allHumans` is built from `byType[EntityType.Human]` plus newborn entities (humanTick.ts:198-208) with no `isPlayerHuman` filter, while every other social list in the file filters it (`playerHumans` at :116, `isPlayerHuman` at :212, :330, :409). The value is fed to `getSchoolAgeMultiplier(entity, updatedBuildings, nurturingSettlerCount)` (humanTick.ts:298), whose contract is education.ts:78-79 `// Nurturing settlers in the village help every child mature a bit faster. const nurtureBoost = Math.min(0.2, nurturingCount * 0.04);`.
impact: Up to three visiting/rival 'nurturing' settlers (entityFactory.ts:74 rolls traits for every human, including visitors, rivals and caravan carriers) contribute up to +0.12 to every colony child's maturation multiplier while they stand in the valley, silently shortening childhood based on who happens to be visiting.
fix: Filter to colony settlers: `allHumans.filter((h) => h.alive && isPlayerHuman(h) && !h.isJuvenile && h.traits?.includes('nurturing'))`.
verification: All three call sites (humanTick.ts:948, 1036, 1209, inside tickHumans 161-1503) omit the 7th argument, so canPursueSecretAffair uses its default `getWorkSchedule({ workSchedule: undefined })` = DEFAULT_WORK_SCHEDULE {7,16} (humanRelationships.ts:1314-1321, workSchedule.ts:4-5,21-24) even though `workSchedule` is already computed in the same function at humanTick.ts:186. isWorkScheduleHour (workSchedule.ts:132-134) then judges work hours from the legacy window, so hours 07:00-08:00 count as work and e.g. 15:00 is treated as work for a 09:00-15:00 colony, diverging from the daily owner, which deliberately passes getWorkSchedule(state) (humanRelationships.ts:1361). Fix: pass `workSchedule` as the 7th argument at 948, 1036 and 1209. Low severity: the divergence only shifts tryst feasibility/feedback in the staggered path, not affair establishment (daily owner).

title: Velocity is blended twice in the hangWithCompany leisure branch (0.45/0.55 then 0.5/0.5 in the shared tail), so company-following movement uses a different weight than every other leisure kind
evidence: humanTick.ts:1293-1294 (inside `if (hangWithCompany && company)`) `entity.vx = entity.vx * 0.45 + idleVx * 0.55; entity.vy = entity.vy * 0.45 + idleVy * 0.55;`, then the chain is followed by the shared tail humanTick.ts:1441-1442 `entity.vx = entity.vx * 0.5 + idleVx * 0.5; entity.vy = entity.vy * 0.5 + idleVy * 0.5;` which is still inside the `if (!suppressIdle) {` block opened at humanTick.ts:1197 and therefore also runs for the company branch (idleVx/idleVy are non-zero there).
impact: The tail re-applies the blend, so a settler walking with partner/child/coworker moves with an effective idle weight of 0.55*0.5 + 0.5 = 0.775 instead of the intended 0.55 (other leisure kinds get 0.5), and `spriteAngle` is computed twice from two different velocity vectors. Company-following steering is therefore much stronger/more snap-to-target than every other idle behaviour, i.e. the branch does not do what its own 0.45/0.55 line implies.

verification: The `hangWithCompany && company` branch (humanTick.ts:1229-1298) blends at 0.45/0.55 and sets suppressIdle, but the shared tail at 1440-1445 sits inside the `if (!suppressIdle)` block opened at line 1197 (before suppressIdle was set), so it blends again at 0.5/0.5 whenever idleVx/idleVy are non-zero — effective idle weight 0.775 versus 0.5 for other leisure kinds, plus a redundant spriteAngle write. Minimal fix: delete lines 1293-1297 and let the shared tail perform the single blend. Impact is a snappier response, not a different destination.

title: isValidHuntingSpotPrey uses `in`, so Object.prototype keys validate as prey ids
evidence:
huntingSpots.ts:34:
  return typeof value === 'string' && value in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP;
impact: PREY_OPTIONS_MAP is a plain object literal, so `'toString' in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP`, `'constructor' in ...` and `'__proto__' in ...` are all true. The worker command boundary uses this as its only guard (simWorker/commands.ts:237 `return isFiniteNumber(cmd.buildingId) && isValidHuntingSpotPrey(cmd.prey);`), so a crafted `setHuntingSpotPrey` command carrying `prey: 'toString'` is accepted and stored on the building via buildingConfigurationActions.ts:109; dailyBuildingEconomy.ts:380 then compares `building.huntingSpotPrey ?? 'auto'` against real prey types, so the post silently harvests nothing, and getHuntingSpotPreyOption('constructor') returns Object.prototype.constructor (UI reads `.label`/`.hint` as undefined).
fix: Use an own-property check: `return typeof value === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value);` (or `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value)`).
verification: huntingSpots.ts:34 is `typeof value === 'string' && value in PREY_OPTIONS_MAP`, and `in` walks the prototype chain, so 'toString'/'constructor' pass, and getHuntingSpotPreyOption would then return the inherited function (line 29's `??` does not catch it). It is the command-channel validator (simWorker/commands.ts:237) while the domain transition rejects the same value (buildingConfigurationActions.ts:99 against VALID_PREY_IDS, lines 15-17), so validation and execution disagree — but the command is simply discarded, hence low. Minimal fix: `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(PREY_OPTIONS_MAP, value)`.

(48-54 createEntity(EntityType.Deer, x, y, ...) — no isPassableWildlifePosition check anywhere in spawnHerdAtEdge)

title: Every herd death is reported and accounted as 'hunted'
evidence:
81:    const killed = active.spawned - alive;
85:      addBigNews(state, '🦌 The herds remember', `${killed} deer taken from the passing herd — next autumn will bring fewer.`, 'negative');
impact: `alive` counts surviving tagged deer, so a deer killed by wolves, a predator, or any non-player cause is counted as taken and permanently shrinks migrationNextHerdSize (line 84). Concrete scenario: the player never hunts, wolves thin the passing herd by three, and the player still gets the negative 'the herds remember ... 3 deer taken' news plus a smaller herd next autumn, while the header comment ('let them pass and next autumn brings them back, fat as ever') and the log text ('herd deer hunted') describe a player hunt that never happened.
fix: Count only player-caused kills (e.g. record a hunted count when markWildlifeDead is invoked from a hunter for an entity with migrationTag === active.herdYear), or reword the news/log to 'deer lost from the passing herd' and leave the size memory keyed on that number deliberately.
verification: tickMigration (migration.ts:66-93) computes `killed = active.spawned - alive` from the tagged deer still present in `state.entities`, so a deer lost to a predator — wolves/foxes/moon howlers catch deer in tickLayerSystems.ts:478-507 — is counted as taken, permanently lowers migrationNextHerdSize (line 84) and produces the 'N deer taken from the passing herd' news plus the 'herd deer hunted' log, contradicting the module's 'let them pass … fat as ever' promise. Minimal fix: record a hunted count only for player-caused kills (hunter path with migrationTag === active.herdYear), or reword the news/log to 'deer lost from the passing herd'. Small magnitude, but a genuine mismatch.

title: transformToWerewolfForm clears assignment ids but only detaches building occupants when `buildings` is passed
evidence:
moonHowler.ts:161  `    && hourOfDay === NIGHT_START`
moonHowler.ts:163  `    && rng() < MOON_HOWLER_REPLACEMENT_CHANCE`
moonHowler.ts:1016  `  if (shouldApplyNewMoonHowlerCurse(colonyDay, hourOfDay, humanPop, activeMoonCurses, rng)) {`  (called from tickLayerRealtime.ts:97 on EVERY tick)

Nothing latches the roll: the only guard is `activeCursed === 0`, which a failed roll does not change, and tickMoonHowlerCycle runs once per tick via tickLayerRealtime. A quiet full moon therefore gets three independent 15% rolls: P = 1 - 0.85^3 = 38.6% per full moon, i.e. ~10 replacement Howlers per 360-day year instead of the ~3.9/year implied by the constant (and the ~1-2/year the comment at lines 78-84 claims). title: tickMoonHowlerCycle's injectable rng is not forwarded to the church rite or the flavour picks
evidence:

(compared with moonHowler.ts:952 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,` and moonHowler.ts:642 `  rng: () => number = Math.random,`)
impact: tickMoonHowlerCycle accepts an injected `rng` but only uses it for the replacement roll (line 1016). The rite path opened here falls back to the default Math.random for the weighted cure/kill/flee roll (line 743), the per-guard save rolls (line 780), the flee-position jitter (line 827) and the four WEREWOLF_*_LINES picks (lines 990, 1030, 1034, 1048). A caller that injects a deterministic stream to make a full-moon cycle reproducible (the seam documented in SIMULATION_AUTHORITY §11 step 4 and in CHANGELOG.md:626-628, and used by tests/moonHowler.rare.test.ts:164-213) cannot control whether the priest is cured or killed, so the 'deterministic full moon' guarantee only covers the replacement roll.

The existing rare-cycle tests pass `[]` buildings so the cure path never runs, and the production caller (tickLayerRealtime.ts:97) passes no rng, so the only impact is the documented deterministic-test seam (SIMULATION_AUTHORITY section 11 step 4). title: getPathGrid cache key omits the map preset, although tiles (and therefore blocked cells) depend on it
evidence: 269: `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(128, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));` (comment 268: "Sub-tile sampling steps prevent tunneling through 1-tile diagonal obstacles")
impact: `TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE` is 10 (gameTypes.ts:992) and the intended step is 5px, but the 128 cap makes the real spacing span/128: 11.7px for a full medium-map line (1200x900 -> span ~1500px) and ~25px on a huge map (2560x1920 -> span ~3200px), i.e. larger than the tile itself. A 1-tile river or mountain strip can fall between two samples, so `lineCrossesBlocked` returns false, `steerWithPath` returns 'direct' (316/349) and the human walks straight through water/mountain — the exact failure the module was written to prevent. Humans have no terrain collision (only wildlife has the deep-water guard, tickLayerSystems.ts:609-628), so nothing downstream corrects it.
fix: Raise the cap so the step can never exceed half a tile (and the tile width for every supported map size), e.g. `const steps = Math.max(4, Math.min(1024, Math.ceil(span / (TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE * 0.5))));`.
verification: getPathGrid keys its module-global cache on `${seed}|${bldSig}|${width}x${height}` (pathfinding.ts:65) while blocked cells are derived from map.tiles (72-77), which terrainGen.ts generates per preset (PRESET_MODIFIERS, waterLevel/mountainThreshold/river carving at 389-434); other map caches do include the preset (terrainLayer.ts:336,367, pixiTerrain.ts:166, terrain.ts:132). restoreWorldMapFromSave regenerates a compact save from seed+preset (saveLoad.ts:163-173) and WorldMap.preset exists (gameTypes.ts:987), so a stale grid would be reused and pathCache would not even clear (setCurrentPathMap compares object identity, pathfinding.ts:286-292). Downgraded to low because no production path reaches the collision: initGame's seed is random unless explicitly passed (worldGen.ts:568) and no in-repo caller passes one (App.tsx:120, App.tsx:892), so two same-seed/different-preset maps cannot arise in normal play. Fix: include `map.preset` in the cache key.

title: Friendship map keys are never pruned, so dead settlers keep counting as friends and boosting energy
evidence: 193: `for (const val of Object.values(p.friendships)) {` … 201: `p.energy = Math.min(maxEnergy, currentEnergy + boost);` — no liveness check, unlike the feud loop's 153: `if (!other) { delete feuds[key]; continue; }`
impact: The feud half of the same function explicitly deletes records whose counterpart is no longer among the living (`byId`), but nothing prunes `friendships` — reconcileFamilyReferencesAfterRemoval clears partner/affair/children links only. A survivor therefore keeps every dead friend's score and keeps collecting up to +2 energy/day from them forever ('Strong friends lift each other's spirits'), and each settler's friendship record grows monotonically as roommates and co-workers die. friendCount() (45-52) likewise counts dead friends.
fix: In the same daily pass, delete friendship keys whose counterpart is missing from `byId` (mirroring the feud cleanup) and compute `strongCount` only over living counterparts.
verification: advanceSocialRelationships prunes feuds for missing partners (relationships.ts:150-156) but the strong-friendship loop (lines 189-203) counts every friendship key >= 60 without consulting the byId map built from living people (line 73), so a dead friend keeps contributing to strongCount and its key is never deleted; the daily energy boost is min(2, strongCount * 0.8) at line 200, so the effect is real but saturates once three strong keys exist. The finding overstates one detail: friendCount (line 45) and activeFeudCount (line 55) have no callers anywhere, so the 'UI badges' half has no consumer. Minimal fix: resolve each key against byId inside the strong-friendship loop and delete or skip missing settlers, mirroring the feud cleanup.

title: The pickSharedResidenceForFamily fallback in assignFamilyToResidence is unreachable
evidence: residencyReconciliation.ts:130-131 `const picked = pickResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy)\n    ?? pickSharedResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy);` — residencySelection.ts:631-633 and 582-584 show both functions skip leader houses and require the identical `familyFitsInResidence(family, residence, humans, occupancy)` predicate before a residence can become `best`.
impact: For any non-empty family, whenever `pickResidenceForFamily` yields `undefined` the second call iterates the same residences with the same fit test and unchanged occupancy and also yields `undefined`, so the right-hand side can never contribute a placement; the `??` branch is dead and hides the fact that a family that fits nowhere is handled entirely by the split path below (adults individually, children by custodian). (Only a zero-length family — never produced by buildHousingUnits or syncPartnerResidence — could make the two disagree, via pickResidenceForFamily's `family.length === 0` early return.)
fix: Delete the `?? pickSharedResidenceForFamily(family, alive, residences, occupancy)` fallback (and the now-unused import/private helper if nothing else uses it), or change one of the two scorers so the fallback expresses a real policy difference.
verification: pickResidenceForFamily (residencySelection.ts:600-680) skips only leader houses, requires the same `familyFitsInResidence` predicate and always sets `best` when any residence passes, so for a non-empty family it returns undefined exactly when no residence fits — the same condition that makes pickSharedResidenceForFamily (residencySelection.ts:573-598) return undefined. buildHousingUnits (residencySelection.ts:248-291) always starts a unit with `collectOwnHousehold`, which unconditionally adds the living seed, so units are never empty and the `??` branch at residencyReconciliation.ts:130-131 can never contribute. title: auditHousingSharingIssues/isUnnecessarilySharingHousing (and residenceHasCapacity) have no callers, and the dead audit counts rival and leader residences as empty housing

title: recentSourceKind scans from the oldest end of a newest-first log and records the wrong source event
evidence: 81 comment: `* Scans backwards through the event log to find the most recent matching event category.`; 85: `const scanLimit = Math.max(0, log.length - 40);`; 87: `for (let i = log.length - 1; i >= scanLimit; i--) {`. Because logEvent unshifts (eventLog.ts:23), index log.length-1 is the OLDEST entry, so the loop walks entries len-40..len-1 (the 41 oldest) and returns the first match found from that end.
impact: The rumour's subject and text (59-65, 134) come from the colony's earliest events instead of the newest: a birth, combat or scandal that just happened is ignored in favour of day-1 scaffolding, so the card narrates stale history. Line 124 compounds it: `[FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT]: state.eventLog[state.eventLog.length - 1]?.id ?? 0` stores the oldest entry's id, not the matched event, and no code ever reads FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT (only the declaration at 28 and this write exist).

verification: logEvent unshifts (eventLog.ts:23), so index log.length-1 is the OLDEST entry, yet recentSourceKind (rumourLedger.ts:87) walks from log.length-1 down to log.length-40 and returns the first match — the 41 oldest events — contradicting its own comment, so the rumour category (and therefore RUMOUR_TEXT, line 59-65) is chosen from ancient history; line 124 likewise stores the oldest entry's id and nothing ever reads FLAG_SOURCE_EVENT (grep finds only the declaration and this write). Minimal fix: iterate from index 0 up to min(len,40) to scan the newest entries, return the matched entry, and store its id; severity low because only one story card's flavour text is affected.

title: economyLedger/foodHistory are written by the tick but missing from the worker rollback backup
evidence: `SimPrepKeys` (L10-87) lists `resources`, `storageMax`, `villageForge`, `researchProgress`, … but not `economyLedger` or `foodHistory`; `extractSimPrep` copies only those keys (e.g. L116 `resources: { ...state.resources },` L117 `storageMax: { ...state.storageMax },`) and `applySimPrep` restores only them (L185-265). Meanwhile the daily tick writes them: economyLedger.ts:47 `state.economyLedger = { day, produced: {}, consumed: {} };` / L56 `ledger.produced[source] = (ledger.produced[source] ?? 0) + amount;` / L31-39 push into `state.foodHistory`. The backup is used to undo an already-applied tick: gameWorker.ts:314 `const prepBackup = extractSimPrep(world);` … L345 `applySimPrep(world, prepBackup);` ('Render buffer pool exhausted').
impact: That rollback restores resources/entities but leaves the rolled-back tick's ledger entries in place. The same tick is then retried (or simply lost), so `ledger.produced`/`consumed` and the archived `foodHistory` day double-count or claim food that was never kept — the exact numbers the Food ledger, dashboard 'Food today' (dashboardData.ts:269-279) and the 30-day history display. Same class of gap applies to `foodSpoilageRate`, which the tick would write once updateStorageCaps is wired in.
fix: Add `'economyLedger' | 'foodHistory' | 'foodSpoilageRate'` to `SimPrepKeys` and clone them in `extractSimPrep` (e.g. `economyLedger: state.economyLedger ? { day: state.economyLedger.day, produced: { ...state.economyLedger.produced }, consumed: { ...state.economyLedger.consumed } } : undefined`, `foodHistory: state.foodHistory ? state.foodHistory.map((s) => ({ ...s, produced: { ...s.produced }, consumed: { ...s.consumed } })) : undefined`) and assign them back in `applySimPrep`.
verification: SimPrepKeys (10-87) and extractSimPrep/applySimPrep omit economyLedger, foodHistory and foodSpoilageRate, while the daily tick writes the first two (economyLedger.ts:47, 56 and 31-39) and gameWorker.ts takes extractSimPrep as a rollback backup at line 314 and restores it at 339/345/355 (buffer-pool and exception paths). The rollback therefore restores resources/entities but leaves the failed tick's ledger entries and archived food sample in place, so the Food ledger and dashboard 'Food today' over-report one tick's worth of production and consumption. Minimal fix: add the three keys to SimPrepKeys and clone/restore them (the foodSpoilageRate part is speculative — updateStorageCaps currently has no caller).

title: Prep backup shallow-clones entities, so nested fields survive a failed-command rollback
evidence: L102-103: `// Clone entity objects shallowly to decouple from in-place property mutations` / `entities: (state.entities ?? []).map((e) => ({ ...e })),`
impact: The backup shares every nested object with the live world, so in-place nested mutations are not rolled back: `ensureEntitySkills(human)[job] = ...` (workforce.ts:211 and 264, skills.ts:37, apprenticeships.ts:95) mutates the shared `skills` map, `parent.childrenIds.push(childId)` (humanLifecycle.ts:40) the shared array, and moon-howler save/restore rewrites the shared `moonHowlerSaved`. gameWorker.ts:222-233 then rolls back via `applySimPrep` and answers `commandResult ok:false` with `safeExtractCommandDelta`, so the surviving mutations are shipped to the main thread as authoritative. The same O(entities) backup is also taken on every tick (gameWorker.ts:314) even though a tick error always ends the worker session (GameLoop.fallbackFromWorker), so the tick-path backup never changes the outcome.
fix: Also copy the mutable nested fields in the entity clone, e.g. `({ ...e, skills: e.skills ? { ...e.skills } : e.skills, childrenIds: e.childrenIds ? [...e.childrenIds] : e.childrenIds, moonHowlerSaved: e.moonHowlerSaved ? { ...e.moonHowlerSaved } : e.moonHowlerSaved })`.
verification: Verified the code fact: extractSimPrep maps entities with `{ ...e }` (103) and only deep-copies buildings' occupants/hotelGuestIds (106-110), so nested entity objects (skills, childrenIds, moonHowlerSaved) are shared, and the cited in-place writers exist (ensureEntitySkills in skills.ts:36-37, childrenIds pushes in humanLifecycle). The described harm is not demonstrated, though: every command that reaches those helpers deep-clones the world first via structuredClone (e.g. buildingStaffingActions.ts:119/216, settlerInteractionActions.ts:69), the in-place routed commands touch only top-level state (guidedCampaign.ts:109-130, visitorQuest.ts:53-64), and a tick error discards the worker entirely (gameWorker.ts:355-356 -> GameLoop.fallbackFromWorker, gameLoop.ts:348-351, 385-404), so the per-tick backup at gameWorker.ts:314 is indeed wasted work. Minimal fix for robustness: copy the mutable nested fields in the clone, or drop the tick-path backup.
alsoReportedAs: Rollback snapshot shallow-copies object slices that the sim mutates in place, so applySimPrep cannot restore them (X5-persistence-worker)

title: syncTreeGrid rebuilds only when the grid object is replaced; a reused tree grid is never reconciled

Because findClosestInEntityGrid (simQueries.ts:113-121) ignores the fallback array whenever a grid exists, trees added later are invisible to humanTick.ts:1404-1412 and blueberryForaging.ts:94-102 — and contrary to the finding's note, nature_boom's 15 trees (groupEvents.ts:1738-1743) do land in `state.entities` via gameTick.ts:234, so this is an observable miss, not a latent one. Minimal fix: add `else grid.reconcile(treeEntities, isTreeGridEntity)`.

title: Unused grid API: forEachNeighborCell, ensurePresent, hasEntity, distSq, buildGrassGrid, buildMobileGrid

title: buildings.upgraded subtracts last year's per-year upgrade count from a cumulative total
evidence:
stats.ts:83-86 `const currentUpgrades = state.buildings.reduce(` / `(sum, b) => sum + (b.level > 1 ? b.level - 1 : 0),` / `0,` / `);`
stats.ts:87 `const prevUpgrades = prevYearStats?.buildings.upgraded ?? 0;`
stats.ts:88 `const upgradesThisYear = Math.max(0, currentUpgrades - prevUpgrades);`
stats.ts:114 `upgraded: upgradesThisYear,`
stats.ts:138 `s.totalBuildingsUpgraded += latestYear.buildings.upgraded;`
impact: `currentUpgrades` is a cumulative total of all upgrade levels in the village, while the field it is compared against (`buildings.upgraded`) is written as that year's *increase* (line 114) and read again as a level. Example: 2 upgrades in year 0 (cumulative 2, recorded 2); no upgrades in year 1 -> 2-2 = 0 (correct); no upgrades in year 2 -> 2-0 = 2 reported (phantom). `updateLifetimeStats` accumulates these into `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded`, which drifts and over-counts. Contrast `marriages`, which correctly uses the previous snapshot `prevYearStats.marriedCount`.
fix: Give YearlyStats a cumulative baseline (`upgradedTotal: currentUpgrades`) and use `const prevUpgrades = prevYearStats?.upgradedTotal ?? 0;`, keeping `upgraded` as the per-year delta; or drop the subtraction and increment `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded` at the upgrade owner.
verification: recordYearlyStats (stats.ts) sums `b.level - 1` over all buildings (lines 83-86), i.e. a cumulative upgrade count, but line 87 subtracts `prevYearStats.buildings.upgraded`, which stores the previous year's *delta* (line 114). Year 0 stores C0 and year 1 is therefore still correct, but every year ≥2 computes `C_n − delta_{n-1}` and `updateLifetimeStats` (line 138) adds that inflated value to `lifetimeStats.totalBuildingsUpgraded`. Minimal fix: persist the cumulative total (e.g. `buildings.upgradedTotal`) and subtract that; impact stays low because grep shows no renderer or other consumer of `totalBuildingsUpgraded`.

title: connectionsAt's 'lone crossing' repair guard can never fire
evidence: lines 166-174: `north: north || (!south && !north), south, east: east || (!west && !east), west,` … `if (countConnections(conn) < 2) { return { north: true, east: true, south: false, west: false }; }`.
